title: Robot Hand Walks, Types and Plays Games on Its Fingers
summary:
Halloween is near, and engineers have built a robot hand that looks like Thing, the creepy walking hand from The Addams Family. This fully articulated hand can balance on its own fingertips and creep around. It also has enough finesse to tap keyboard keys, push small objects and even play a basic computer game while balancing on its remaining fingers.

This is not the first walking robot hand. Past efforts mostly worked, but they required changing the hand's structure so every finger was the same length, which was a significant design compromise. Human hands are defined by uneven fingers and an opposite thumb. That asymmetry helps us handle many tools, but it is not well suited for upright walking.

A team from the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich in Switzerland set out to solve this very specific problem. They describe their work in a recent preprint, a paper that has not undergone peer review or been accepted for publication in a scientific journal. The team started with an off-the-shelf mechanical hand designed for humanoid robots, with five fingers and 20 actuated joints. Then they added a battery, several motion sensors and a tiny computer to the back of the robot. With these additions, the whole thing weighs 1.8 pounds.

Next, the team taught the hand to balance, a first step toward walking. They trained it in a simulation environment using reinforcement learning, where the software rewarded the hand every time it correctly balanced on its uneven fingers. The training also taught the software each finger's unique timing.

The team then put the hand through real-world field tests. The hand traversed 14 different indoor and outdoor environments with a variety of surface textures. It moved across carpet, gravel, grass and metal with a springy, spider-like gait. The robot hand could also balance on several fingers while using the remaining ones to push a small cube forward or type on a keyboard. In testing, it correctly hit keys 29 out of 32 times. It was even able to play the puzzle-solving video game Sokoban by pressing the correct arrow keys in sequence.

The team notes that these features may serve a more important purpose than making a Halloween decoration. In the future, humanoid robots working in cramped areas could reach toward a spot they cannot get to, detach their hand and send it crawling off to retrieve an item. That is an unsettling image, but it could also mean the end of annoyingly lost screwdrivers. "Giving robotic hands their own mobility could make future robots more versatile in the spaces and interfaces built for people," the researchers write in the paper.
why_it_matters: Giving robot hands their own mobility could help future robots work in spaces and with tools made for people, as the researchers suggest.

keywords.explanation: A science paper that has not yet been checked by other scientists or published in a journal.
Ready-made and already available to buy.
Joints that are moved by motors.
A way to teach software by giving rewards for good results.
The way a person or robot walks.
Robots built to have a human-like shape.

questions.question: Why was it a design compromise to make every finger the same length?
options: Human hands naturally have uneven fingers and an opposite thumb
It made the fingers too short to reach a keyboard
It meant the hand could only be built at night
It made the hand unable to hold any battery
questions.correct_answer: Human hands naturally have uneven fingers and an opposite thumb

questions.question: Which parts did the team add to the back of the mechanical hand?
options: A camera, a speaker and a small screen
A battery, several motion sensors and a tiny computer
A solar panel, a wheel and a light bulb
A motor, a spring and a set of tools
questions.correct_answer: A battery, several motion sensors and a tiny computer

questions.question: How was the software rewarded during training?
options: Every time the hand walked faster than it had before
Every time a person pressed a button on a keyboard
Every time the hand correctly balanced on its uneven fingers
Every time the hand picked up a heavy object
questions.correct_answer: Every time the hand correctly balanced on its uneven fingers

questions.question: How did the hand move across carpet, gravel, grass and metal?
options: With a smooth slide like an ice skater
With a slow rolling motion on wheels
With long jumps like a kangaroo
With a springy, spider-like gait

questions.question: Which video game did the hand play?
options: A racing game played with a toy steering wheel
A word game played with the whole alphabet
A music game played by hitting a drum pad
Sokoban, by pressing the correct arrow keys in sequence
questions.correct_answer: Sokoban, by pressing the correct arrow keys in sequence

questions.question: What possible future use does the team describe?
options: A robot hand that helps visitors find a way in a museum
A robot that teaches new students how to type on keyboards
A humanoid robot detaching its hand to retrieve an item from a cramped spot
A robot using its hand to paint pictures at a home
questions.correct_answer: A humanoid robot detaching its hand to retrieve an item from a cramped spot
